---
title: "In general, when your software contributes to a paper, are you acknowledged in that paper?"
question_id: paper2mod
---

```{r}
#| include: false
#| file: ../R/_load_common.R
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
question_code <- "paper2mod"

nordic_countries <- c(
  "Finland", "Norway", "Sweden", "Denmark", "Iceland", "Estonia"
)
country_groups <- list(
  Nordics = nordic_countries,
  Germany = "Germany",
  Netherlands = "Netherlands"
)
plot_countries <- countries_from_groups(country_groups)
```

## Nordics

### Descriptive Statistics

```{r}
#| echo: false

print_heatmap_category_table(
  FILTER,
  question_code,
  header = "In general, when your software contributes to a paper, are you acknowledged in that paper? (Nordics)"
)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10

plot_heatmap(FILTER, question_code, title = "Nordics")
```

### Free-text responses

```{r}
#| echo: false
source(file.path(book_root, "R/recodes/paper2mod_recode.R"))

cleaned_data <- process_text_codes_with_allocation(
  filter = FILTER,
  question_code = "paper2mod",
  recode_map = paper2mod_recode_map,
  header = "In general, when your software contributes to a paper, are you acknowledged in that paper?",
  other = TRUE,
  cache_id = "paper2mod"
)

cleaned_data$summary_table
```

The raw-to-category allocation table for this question is in @sec-appendix-recoding.

## Within Nordics

```{r}
#| echo: false

print_heatmap_category_table(
  nordic_countries,
  question_code,
  header = "In general, when your software contributes to a paper, are you acknowledged in that paper? within Nordic countries",
  group_by = nordic_countries
)
```

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6

plot_heatmap_category_stacked_bars(
  nordic_countries,
  question_code,
  countries = nordic_countries,
  title = "In general, when your software contributes to a paper, are you acknowledged in that paper? within Nordic countries"
)
```

## Between Countries

```{r}
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 10
#| fig-height: 6

plot_heatmap_category_stacked_bars(

)
```
